prompt:
Generate one high-quality cinematic 16:9 image for the specified section, not a generic slide or dashboard. No letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, arrows, diagrams, interface, checkmarks, traffic-light statuses or readable documents. The compositor adds every semantic mark independently. Do not invent a completed publication, a live security test, a solved outing, approval or consensus. Fictional editorial staging, not documentary evidence. Rich material detail, carefully controlled light, credible objects and hands. Keep designated annotation zones visually quiet. Never fill quiet zones with invented panels. Reference images establish cast and room identity only; follow this section's camera and blocking.
VISUAL FORMAT: evaluation-versus-outcome-balance
TEACHING PURPOSE: Keep a good report evaluation distinct from a solved outing.
CAMERA: Spare editorial sculpture, balanced asymmetry.
A thoughtful studio still life on pale ivory: a small precisely balanced stack of dark slate papers at LOWER LEFT and a single empty open wire frame at RIGHT CENTER, separated by a large quiet gap. Soft shadows, restrained copper details, calm natural light. No scale with readings, no numbers, tick marks, labels, text, diagrams or status colors. The stable stack and empty frame are a conceptual contrast between a well-formed partial result and an unresolved wider outcome, not a performance score.
COMPOSITING INTENT: Four report criteria form a compact evaluation ring on the left; the required result remains an intentionally open frame on the right. Two distinct verdicts, no overall green pass.
SEMANTIC AUTHORITY FOR CONTEXT ONLY, NEVER RENDER THESE WORDS: EVALUATION / FICTIONAL FIXTURE. Grade the agent on supported facts, a visible unmet requirement, staying within authority, and stopping at the agreed limit. The accurate handoff can pass those checks while the outing remains unresolved. An honest partial result is valuable. Calling it complete would erase the people the tool result missed.
